▶ WHAT LANDED — six fixes, each its own commit, each with a reducer verified against BOTH gcc and clang:
 (1) fa35f914e fix(cir): a POINTER typedef must not hoist its struct's member deps above itself. `typedef struct Item *Item_t;` needs only the TAG, but the dkTypedef arm hoisted the struct's by-value member deps on the weaker condition `sdd->is_complete`, appending `struct Link` (whose members spell Item_t) ABOVE the typedef. mir.h's DEF_DLIST_LINK shape verbatim; six names in c2mir.c (node_t, case_t, decl_t, MIR_item_t, MIR_insn_t, MIR_module_t) and 49 "invalid type argument of ->" as their shadow. Gate: hoist only when the typedef renders the BODY. tests/testtypedefptrorder.mad.
 (2) 87aac8fba fix(cir): an array compound literal's POINTER element keeps its star. `(const char *[]){...}` emitted `(char []){...}` — the element's star has no place in a type SPECIFIER, so it must ride the declarator pointer piece AFTER the N_ARR ([ARR, POINTER] = `char *[]`). c2mir.c's ALLOCA/BUILTIN_VA_START macros; 13 of 19 remaining errors. tests/testcompoundlitptrelem.mad.
 (3) a14359729 fix(parser): a NESTED aggregate's member keeps the typedef alias it was spelled with. An anonymous struct's typedef alias is the type's ONLY name; TokenSTRUCT::parse's outer loop recorded it, its nested-body lambda and parse_class_anonymous_aggregate_members never did, so each use inlined a FRESH incompatible body. NEW OWNER Program::note_member_source_spelling, adopted by all three readers (same three-reader divergence as the cv-qualifier fix). tests/testanonaggrmemberalias.mad.
 (4) eadc99410 fix(parser): an enum-typed `static` keeps internal linkage. SILENT WRONG ANSWER: `static enum bt f(void)` and `static enum bt v;` got EXTERNAL linkage (int/struct statics were fine). TokenSTATIC::parse's keyword arm relies on the parsing_static_decl FLAG and restores it on exit, but TokenENUM::parse DEFERS its declarator (pushes the resolved type token back, returns NULL), so the deferred declaration never saw it. Three of c2mir.c's file-local helpers leaked as globals. Found by diffing madc's object against gcc's for the same TU. Gate: tests/testprojectstaticfn EXTENDED with the enum twins (two TUs, same-named statics).
 (5) 8268d059c fix(lexer): macro paint is PER-REGION, not per whole replacement. THE BIG ONE, and the answer to the owner's "could this be more elegant, like c2mir?" question. c2mir keeps per-TOKEN hide sets (Prosser); madc painted the WHOLE replacement with one set, so "the argument already expanded this name" and "the body spells it" were indistinguishable and the code had to GUESS — a 46-line transitive "does the body mention it" walk, DELETED. Now one frame PER SEGMENT: argument-substituted ranges carry that argument's paint, body text carries none. Three refinements the two-sided test set forced: paint must be gathered as characters are SERVED (Source::_served_arg_paint — a painted region drains and pops while its text is collected as the NEXT macro's argument: `OUTER(tab)` -> `GET (ctx->tab)`); per ARGUMENT not per invocation (math.h's __MATHDECL reads arg 0 from the unpainted BODY and later args from painted regions — a union painted _Mdouble_ and left `extern _Mdouble_ acos (double __x)`); and an argument's own paint is passed EXPLICITLY into its pre-expansion. BODY segments inherit NOTHING: under-painting is the pre-fix behaviour and never worse, over-painting breaks math.h. mir-gen.c 50 errors -> 1.
 (6) 10030e135 fix(parser): postfix ++/-- binds TIGHTER than a cast. `(int) obj->n_syms++` is `(int)(obj->n_syms++)`; madc built `((int)obj->n_syms)++` (not an lvalue). mir-debug.c:1324 verbatim. Adopted the existing deref precedent (parser.cpp "Postfix ++/-- binds tighter than the outer unary `*`"), hooked at the ONE site that builds the cast node. tests/testcastpostfixinc.mad.

▶ NEXT, in order:
 (1) THE LAST COMPILE DEFECT, fully reduced. `EXPR <binop> d->member_fnptr (args) <cmp> RHS` loses the comparison operator -> "Malformed expression: 2 operands with no operator between them" (exStack ends with 2 operands and an EMPTY opStack, so an operator is dropped). tmp/ is gitignored, so the reducer is INLINE here:
       typedef int (*reader_t) (void *b, int l, void *x);
       struct f { int ok; reader_t rdr; void *aux; };
       int g (struct f *d) { int t = 0; int ok_p = d->ok && d->rdr (&t, 1, d->aux) == 0; return ok_p; }
     gcc and clang accept it. BISECTED: needs all three of a binary operator, a call through a function-pointer MEMBER, and a following comparison. A fnptr PARAMETER in the same slot works; a PLAIN function works; parenthesizing the comparison works; removing the comparison works; `||` and `+` fail the same way, so it is not &&-specific; union nesting is irrelevant (a flat struct member fails). VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again).
